answer: The design leans on session-key rotation bound to work, forfeited on duplicate submission, auditors are drawn from a rotating pool. The hollow lists finished tasks with their hashes, and the wander is where a second reviewer recomputes them. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. Written in a tight, ends on the cost register, it stays short. Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the beacon of payment, so volume alone buys nothing.
